Reef Portable - Classroom Testing Checklist
============================================
Version: portable Windows x64 build

Copy this entire folder to a USB stick and run Reef.exe on each classroom
machine. Tick each item as verified.

A. PORTABLE INSTALLATION (no install, no admin)
-----------------------------------------------
[ ] Reef.exe is present next to portable.marker
[ ] WebView2Loader.dll is NOT required
[ ] Running Reef.exe does not require administrator elevation
[ ] Reef.exe runs from a USB stick with any drive letter
[ ] Moving the USB stick to a different drive letter still works
[ ] No files are written to %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, or user home
[ ] Config/reef-config.json is created next to Reef.exe
[ ] Data/ directory is created next to Reef.exe

B. DIAGNOSTICS & LOGGING
------------------------
[ ] App starts and writes a startup diagnostics event (Logs/Diagnostics/)
[ ] Logs contain run IDs and millisecond timestamps
[ ] Log levels present: TRACE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR
[ ] JSONL and human-readable log files are both produced
[ ] Log rotation creates part files when a stream exceeds the size cap
[ ] Diagnostics panel shows status, environment, and log list
[ ] A log file can be previewed and copied from the panel
[ ] Log directory can be opened from the panel
[ ] Visible terminal can be cleared without deleting stored logs
[ ] Logs can be exported to a ZIP (written to Logs/Exports/)
[ ] Export ZIP contains environment.json, diagnostics-status.json,
    README.txt, Logs/ (excluding Logs/Exports), Config/reef-config.json
[ ] Old logs rotate and do not grow without bound (512 MiB cap per stream)

C. TERMINAL / SESSION RECORDING
-------------------------------
[ ] Session recording can be started and stopped from the terminal toolbar
[ ] Recording status is shown in the terminal toolbar
[ ] Recorded output is saved under Logs/Sessions/<date>/
[ ] Recording survives and preserves data on unexpected session end
[ ] Large terminal output is not silently lost (full output recorded)
[ ] Ctrl+C (SIGINT) can be sent to the connected device from the toolbar
[ ] Session diagnostics are viewable in the Diagnostics panel

D. SAFETY GUARD - NO STARTUP-CONFIG WRITES (MANDATORY)
-------------------------------------------------------
[ ] `write memory` is blocked and logged
[ ] `write` is blocked and logged
[ ] `copy running-config startup-config` is blocked and logged
[ ] `copy run start` is blocked and logged
[ ] `erase startup-config` / `delete nvram` variants are blocked and logged
[ ] Blocked attempts do NOT expose passwords/secrets in logs
[ ] Normal running-config edits still work (e.g. interface IP change)
[ ] `show running-config` and other show commands still work
[ ] There is no setting to re-enable startup-config writes
[ ] Blocked attempts are visible in the Diagnostics/log output

E. SECRETS & SECURITY
---------------------
[ ] Passwords are not recorded in plain text in logs
[ ] Private keys / tokens are not recorded in plain text in logs
[ ] SSH host-key verification remains enabled (cannot be disabled)
[ ] Redaction applies to known secret keywords

F. WINDOWS x64 BUILD (for the person building the image)
--------------------------------------------------------
[ ] reef.exe is a PE32+ x86-64 GUI executable
[ ] No WebView2Loader.dll required; imports only system DLLs
[ ] Binary compiled with x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target
[ ] dist/Reef-USB.zip contains all files listed above
[ ] Zip extract preserves directory structure and portable.marker

NOTES
-----
- Direct/raw terminal access typed by the user cannot be fully guarded; the
  safety guard covers Reef-managed command paths only.
- No WebView2 Runtime required; the UI is rendered natively by wgpui.
- This is a diagnostic/classroom tool, not a production configuration
  management system.
